title: The Drosophila escape motor circuit shows differential vulnerability to aging linked to functional decay.
source_locator: Results, 'Localizing the neural correlates for aging-related loss of escape behavior'; Fig 4A and 4B; Methods 'Optogenetically-induced escape response'
quote: escape responses can be elicited by a 50 ms red-light flash with ≥80% response probability throughout adult life (Fig 4A, red bars)
mapping_basis: Paper names the giant fiber descending neuron 'GF' (Fig 3A legend: 'GF or DNp01'); synonyms.csv maps GF (literature) to DNp01 only, not ambiguous.
stimulation: red light; Results/Fig 4 legend: 50 ms red-light flash; Methods: three 594 nm red-light pulses of 2 s duration, every 10 s; responder if escape to at least one pulse
sensory_condition: single fly in 9 x 2 cm Petri dish, dim infrared illumination, infrared camera
coordination_notes: Escape = jump (mesothoracic leg extension via TTM) followed by flight, as the paper defines the GF-mediated escape response.
penetrance: >=80% responders at ages 3-60 d; reduced but close to 80% at >60 d (Fig 4A); ~50% of >60 d visual non-responders (Fig 4B); 0% in UAS-GFP controls
n_flies_note: Fig 4A test groups per age bin: 167, 158, 147, 134, 118; Fig 4B: 33 pre-selected >60 d non-responders (36 GFP controls)
notes: Escape scored as a binary behaviour from IR video; no leg tracking. Single ballistic jump/takeoff coded as 'no' rhythm for all legs per PROTOCOL sec. 3 (single movements). Paper calls the split line 'highly specific' / 'only in the GF'. Stimulus duration differs between Results (50 ms flash) and Methods (2 s pulses). Sex: Methods say 'For all experiments male flies were removed at the ages required for experimental testing', read as males tested; slightly ambiguous. Fig 4A and 4B combined into one record (same line, preparation and outcome type). Electrical GF stimulation with TTM/DLM EMG (Figs 2, 4F-J) is not opto/thermogenetic activation and is not recorded.

title: Neuronal control of Drosophila walking direction.
quote: is sufficient to trigger backward walking under conditions in which flies would otherwise walk forward
mapping_basis: Paper's name 'MDN' is the MANC type name in type_list.csv / assigned_types.csv.
notes: Abstract only: full text paywalled (science.org 403; not in PMC/Europe PMC). Sufficiency statement implies an activation experiment, but the abstract names no effector, driver line, stimulus or preparation. effector_kind = 'thermogenetic' is a PLACEHOLDER forced by the schema enum and is NOT supported by any text I read; preparation set to 'other' because it is not stated. Leg rhythm 'yes' for all pairs per walking convention (backward walking). Walking-direction switch from forward to backward has no effect_on_walking vocabulary term; left not_assessed. Context sentence: 'MDN activity is required for flies to walk backward when they encounter an impassable barrier'.
